title: Engine oil and filter due
blurb: Overdue on a lift engine is not the same as overdue on an ordinary one — the VVTL-i lifters are hydraulic, and oil is what operates them.
symptom:
Nothing wrong yet. This one is on the list because of what the engine is.

Why the 2ZZ-GE cares more than most

Lift is engaged by oil pressure pushing a locking pin through a slipper follower. Low, thin or degraded oil means the pin does not lock reliably — and a lift mechanism that half-engages at 6,200 rpm is how these engines destroy a lobe. The usual first symptom is lift that comes in late, inconsistently, or not at all when hot.
cause: Ordinary service interval. Worth doing more often than the book implies on an engine that spends time near 8,000 rpm.

check.t: Check the level on a warm engine, parked level
check.hint: Do this far more often than you change it.

check.t: Look at the colour and feel of the oil
check.hint: The manual says to replace it if the quality is visibly poor, regardless of mileage.

check.t: Note the mileage and date before draining
check.hint: Log it in the garage page afterwards.

check.t: Check whether this car has an oil cooler
check.hint: It changes the fill quantity — 4.4 L with, 4.2 L without.

check.t: Have a new drain plug gasket ready
check.hint: The manual calls for a new one every time.

fix:
Straight out of the manual's own procedure:

  1. Remove the centre engine under cover.
  2. Remove the oil filler cap, then the drain plug, and drain into a container.
  3. Replace the oil filter. Toyota specify SST 09228-06501, and to tighten the new filter a further 3/4 turn after the gasket contacts.
  4. Clean and install the drain plug with a new gasket.
  5. Refill, run, check for leaks, re-check the level.
ItemFigure
Drain plug torque37 N·m — 378 kgf·cm, 27 ft·lbf
Capacity, with oil cooler4.4 L — 4.8 US qt, 4.0 Imp qt
Capacity, without oil cooler4.2 L — 4.6 US qt, 3.8 Imp qt
Dry fill4.8 L — 5.1 US qt, 4.2 Imp qt
GradeAPI SJ / ILSAC, SAE 5W-30 named first choice

Torque and procedure read off LU-3 (p.1070); capacities off PP-17 (p.75). The 5W-30 recommendation is the manual's, written in 1999 — plenty of 2ZZ owners run a heavier grade in summer, which is a judgement call, not a specification.
